newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Fazio sounds warning on bank costs - paper.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Fazio sounds warning on bank costs - paper.

text.p: The governor of the Bank of Italy Antonio Fazio has appealed to the government to help Italy's banks streamline their bloated payrolls and catch up with their European competitors, an Italian newspaper reported on Tuesday.

Il Sole 24 Ore reported that Fazio had sent letters to Prime Minister Romano Prodi, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi and Labour Minister Tiziano Treu warning that labour costs in the Italian banking industry were too high.
Fazio's letter stated that labour costs are 50 percent higher than the European average in the industry, Il Sole reported.
Italy's banks are under pressure from increased competition which is forcing them to reduce margins while they are not at the same time able to cut costs, the newspaper said.

Il Sole said Fazio called on the government to make it easier for the banks to lay off excess personnel by providing special funding and to halt nationwide contracts for bank employees and encourage salary negotiations at company level.
Bank analysts estimate that the industry will have to lay off at least 30,000 employees in the coming years.
A bank employees' contract expires in December 1997 and a contract governing salaries for managers runs out in June 1998.

Massimo D'Alema, the leader of the left-wing PDS party which is the main component of Prodi's centre-left coalition, called on the Bank of Italy on Monday to take a close interest in wage contracts in the banking sector.
D'Alema said banks had to recover their competitive edge because "the idea that the banking system should be protected has made our country pay a high price."
